derived: LLY turned 14.30% of revenue into free cash over 2018 to 2025 against the 38.1% its filed expense lines leave. Restated before interest: LLY paid $3,152mm of interest inside operating cash flow over 2018 to 2025, 1.17% of revenue. The free cash flow above is struck after it and the valuation already charges the debt by subtracting net debt, so the charge falls by that much, from 28.46% to 27.30%. Restated at replacement capex: LLY spent $23,144mm on plant over 2018 to 2025 against $7,255mm of plant depreciation, 5.89% of revenue above what keeps the plant running. Taken at depreciation, the charge falls from 27.30% to 20.25%. Checked without one-off cash: deal payments are booked under investing, so free cash flow never carried them, and no settlement or transition tax is stated for the window, so the charge stands. Restated without working capital build: over 2018 to 2025 LLY's cash flow statement shows receivables up $15,658mm, inventories up $10,223mm, payables and accrued liabilities up $18,257mm, a working capital build of $7,624mm, 2.83% of revenue. Growth ties that cash up once, not on every product for ever, so the charge falls from 20.25% to 16.87%.

column11: judgement: HEART-3 (NCT07839936), the Phase 2, has an estimated primary completion of 2028-08 and no Phase 3 is registered, so a Phase 3 starts late 2028 at the earliest. Leqvio, the last new lipid-lowering modality to reach the US market, went from its first Phase 3 start (ORION-11, NCT03400800, 2017-11-01) to approval on 2021-12-22 (NDA214012, book approvals table) and a first full year in 2022, 4.2 years; late 2028 plus 4.2 years puts the first full year in 2033. Lipfendra went from CORALreef HeFH (NCT05952869, 2023-08-08) to approval on 2026-07-15 (NDA220848) and a first full year in 2027, 3.4 years, which would give 2032
column12: Leqvio is taken over Lipfendra because a first-in-human class of medicine is more likely to need a longer safety file than a fourth PCSK9 agent. Lilly has stated no filing date. The CVR Lilly owes on first US Phase 3 dosing in ASCVD lapses ten years after the 2025 closing (Schedule 14D-9), which sets no date either way

column11: Wholly Lilly's: Lilly FY2025 10-K (0000059478-26-000013), Note 4: in July 2025 Lilly acquired all shares of Verve for $10.50 a share in cash plus one CVR of up to $3.00 a share (about $300mm), and the $608mm of acquired IPR&D 'primarily relate to VERVE-102 (PCSK9 Editor)'. The Beam opt-in rights over the PCSK9 programme were already Lilly's under the 2023 TDA (Verve FY2024 10-K). One upstream royalty is filed as a rate: under the Cas9 License Agreement, Broad and Harvard licensed Verve their Cas9 patent rights for 'products directed to PCSK9, ANGPTL3 and two additional targets', and 'are entitled to receive mid single-digit percentage royalties on net sales of licensed products for the prevention or treatment of human disease' (Verve FY2024 10-K). Netted as the book nets every royalty: mid single-digit read at 4%, its lowest reading, over the 28.6946% pre-tax margin this file's own cost rows leave (1 - 0.1696 - 0.1702 - 0.2046 - 0.168654): 1 - 0.04 / 0.286946 = 0.860601
column12: a ceiling on Lilly's share: read at 5% it is 0.825751, and Verve also paid milestones 'under Beam's third-party agreements' on base-editing technology with no royalty rate stated. The filing lets Verve credit third-party royalties against the Broad and Harvard royalty down to a floor it does not state. Three low single-digit royalties in the same 10-K are quoted and not netted, as the book treats a low single-digit rate: Acuitas, on its LNP licence for the PCSK9 gene target; Novartis, on its non-exclusive lipid licence; and the Harvard/Broad base editing licence, which Note 8 gives as low single digit (whether any covers VERVE-102's GalNAc-LNP is not stated). The CVR is deal cash owed on first US Phase 3 dosing in ASCVD and is not modelled

column12: a company forecast, the weakest kind of anchor the book accepts, and no aggregator or broker peak for VERVE-102 was found. The denominator is the arguable part: 2% is read as a share of the eligible ASCVD stock, not of every patient passing through the pool in 25 years, which would give about 2.7 times this. CROSS-CHECK against the incumbent: the PCSK9 antibodies started about 449,000 Medicare Part D patients in 2025 (Repatha's three presentations and Praluent Pen: 552,415 beneficiaries in 2024 and 693,146 in 2025, drug_demand and the quarterly companion, at the 55.8% Medicare discontinuation Navar et al. report), 2.36% of this pool from Part D alone; this seed starts about 0.06% a year at peak, a fortieth of that. The case for more: a one-time course against lifelong injections, and a 62% LDL-C cut. The case against: no in vivo gene editor is approved for a common disease, a permanent edit has no off switch, and payers will weigh $50,000 upfront against Repatha after its US antibody patent expires on 2029-08-27 (data/disclosed_loe.csv)
